summary_paragraph: A 46-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and obesity was admitted for acute-on-chronic epigastric pain and vomiting due to a gastroparesis flare, just five days after a prior discharge. She was treated with IV fluids, ondansetron, metoclopramide, and pain control with acetaminophen and tramadol. Her blood pressure was elevated likely due to pain, and her A1c was 8.3%, indicating suboptimal diabetes control. She gradually improved, tolerated a full diet, and was discharged home with instructions to maintain strict glucose control, eat small frequent meals, and follow up for persistent leukocytosis. No surgical procedures were performed.
